steps.title: Welcome to Tenali
steps.instruction: Welcome to Tenali. Your products, bills, stock, accounts and own online shop stay together. Let us begin with your AI helper, then walk through everyday tasks at a comfortable pace.
steps.note: All screens use made-up shop details. Pause, use captions or choose any chapter below. No customer data or live AI answers are shown.

steps.title: Ask in ordinary words
steps.instruction: Open Tenali AI and choose New chat. Type what you need in the Message box. You can also ask for help beside your work. AI must be enabled for your business.
steps.note: Your role and enabled features limit what AI can read or prepare. Ask one clear question and check its answer.

steps.title: Review linked work before saving
steps.instruction: For a purchase, ask AI to prepare the supplier, product and bill together. Attach the bill if needed. Review every proposed step, check missing details, then confirm only the work you want saved.
steps.note: This screen shows an example request, not a live AI result. In an actual reply, use Review & check, inspect the changes, then Confirm & save. Not every action is enabled.

steps.title: Make an Excel upload with AI
steps.instruction: To prepare a product list, select Prepare product bulk workbook and attach your catalogue. Download the reply's ZIP. Review its Excel sheet and product pictures, then upload it through Bulk Upload.
steps.note: AI uses the same formatted product template as the upload page. The ZIP contains manifest.xlsx and images. Generated internal SKUs and descriptions need review; tax and prices must be checked.

steps.title: Name your cash or bank account
steps.instruction: In Accounts, give each money account a clear nickname, such as Shop cash or Business bank. Choose its type and enter the opening balance once: the money already there when you start.
steps.note: A money account is not a staff login. Do not enter the same starting money again as a receipt.

steps.title: Check what came in and went out
steps.instruction: Account Tally shows opening money, money received, money paid and the current balance. Compare cash with your counted drawer and bank with your statement. Record an internal transfer once, not as a sale.
steps.note: Use the correct account on each payment. Account transaction and journal filters help you trace a difference.

steps.title: Record money you borrowed
steps.instruction: Open Borrowing and Settlements. Select the contact, choose Borrowed from party, and enter the amount and date. Choose the account receiving the money if you also want its money entry recorded.
steps.note: Borrowing is money you must return, not sales income. Check the linked-account switch before recording so you do not post the same movement twice.

steps.title: Record money you lent
steps.instruction: For money you give someone to return later, choose Lent to party. Select the contact, amount, date and paying account. Review the direction carefully: lending is different from paying a supplier bill.
steps.note: The example amount is INR 2,000. Use Purchases for supplier bills, not this borrowing form.

steps.title: Record a repayment or collection
steps.instruction: When returning borrowed money, choose Repaid to party. When someone returns money you lent, choose Collected from party. Enter only the amount moving today, then check the remaining balance and history.
steps.note: For example, borrowing INR 10,000 and repaying INR 2,500 leaves INR 7,500. Customer invoice collections belong in Receivables & Collections.

steps.title: Enter your supplier's bill
steps.instruction: Open Purchases. Select the vendor, store, bill date and supplier's bill number. Add the products, quantities and buying prices. If you paid something now, enter that amount and the paying account.
steps.note: Buying price is what you pay the supplier, not your selling price. Check tax, totals and the unpaid balance before posting.

steps.title: Add stock when goods arrive
steps.instruction: If all the listed goods have arrived, select Goods received now before posting. Otherwise leave it off and confirm receipt later. Recording a bill and receiving the goods are separate checks.
steps.note: Goods received now adds all product-line quantities to the selected store. Do not also enter those same goods as opening stock. Service receipts do not add product stock.

steps.title: Keep stores separate
steps.instruction: Under Stores and Warehouses, add each shop or warehouse with a short code and clear name. Choose the right store on sales, purchases and stock movements so each location's quantity stays meaningful.
steps.note: A store code is used in document numbers. Use the inventory stock-transfer tool when moving goods between stores, not an extra purchase or sale.

steps.title: Choose where online orders come from
steps.instruction: For an online store, choose Online store as the kind and link its fulfilment shop or warehouse. This is the location supplying those orders. Shops can separately allow customers to collect orders.
steps.note: An online store does not hold a second copy of stock. Set its settlement account and complete checkout setup before taking real payments.

steps.title: Admin is for setting things up
steps.instruction: Open the three-line menu. Admin contains Company Setup, Stores and Warehouses, Users and Roles, Storefront Design, domains, policies, and payment setup. Owners and administrators manage these settings and team access.
steps.note: Do not give a customer your staff login. Team members see only the modules and stores their access permits.

steps.title: Operations is for daily work
steps.instruction: Operations contains your everyday tools: contacts, accounts, borrowing, purchases, sales, receivables, products and reports. The Operations Portal also has start-of-day and closing checklists to help you remember important checks.
steps.note: Menu items depend on your access and enabled features. A checklist is a reminder, not proof that a payment or stock movement happened.

steps.title: Get a quick business check
steps.instruction: On Dashboard, choose the dates and store you want to check. Review sales, money received, unpaid amounts, pending purchases and low stock. Open the relevant work area when a figure needs attention.
steps.note: A total depends on the selected period, store and your permissions. It is not necessarily the balance in your bank.

steps.title: Create your business account
steps.instruction: New to Tenali? Choose Set up my business and a sign-in option, then add your business name and workspace address. Already registered? Choose Sign in and open your existing business instead.
steps.note: Your workspace is your business area in Tenali. Avoid creating a second workspace for the same records by accident.

steps.title: Check your shop and GST details
steps.instruction: In Company Setup, enter your name, address, phone and email. GST off means sales documents have no GST. Turn it on and enter your GSTIN only for a GST-registered business.
steps.note: The GST switch changes documents; it does not register your business for GST. This sample shop uses GST off. Display Name is what customers see.

steps.title: Add a product and its code
steps.instruction: In Product Inventory, choose Add Product. Enter a recognisable name, such as Steel water bottle. SKU is your own short item code; we use BOTTLE-01. Avoid adding the same item twice.
steps.note: An AI-generated SKU is an internal code to review, not a manufacturer's part number.

steps.title: Choose the brand, category and HSN
steps.instruction: Choose or type the brand and category. Select a saved HSN code when needed; its description and GST rate fill from that saved record. Check these values match the product before continuing.
steps.note: HSN groups goods for tax. Selecting a category is not a substitute for checking tax classification.

steps.title: Set the price customers pay
steps.instruction: Choose Keep catalog price and enter 250 in Catalog Price. This is the catalogue selling price for our sample bottle. The supplier's buying price is a different number, recorded with purchases.
steps.note: Other pricing rules can calculate from vendor prices; use the rule that matches your intended selling method and review the result.

steps.title: Add a clear product picture
steps.instruction: Choose a picture file or enter its public image link. Aim for a square, one-thousand-pixel product picture under one megabyte. Choose a background in ordinary colour names. Review, then save the product.
steps.note: PNG, JPEG or WebP. Images fit without stretching. A background change needs an isolated product or transparent image; a low-resolution catalogue cannot gain missing real detail.

steps.title: Enter what you already own
steps.instruction: In Owned Stock, choose the store and Stock In. Enter 24 and the reason Opening stock. Record the movement once. Saving a product alone does not put any physical bottles into stock.
steps.note: Opening stock is what you already have when starting. Do not duplicate quantities already added through a received purchase.

steps.title: Download the right Excel template
steps.instruction: Open Bulk Upload and choose the record type. Download its template, then fill the Data sheet. README explains every column. Use the fresh template to include current dropdown choices and dependent saved details.
steps.note: The Excel file works offline. Its dropdown snapshot does not refresh on every open; download a fresh template after changing your saved lists.

steps.title: Include product, brand and category images
steps.instruction: For web pictures, fill image URL. For local files, enter each filename and ZIP manifest.xlsx with an images folder. Brand and category templates support pictures too. Product rows can include their matching brand and category images.
steps.note: Recommended squares: product 1000×1000, logo 600×600, category 800×800 pixels. Use English background names such as white. Review extracted product crops before importing.

steps.title: Check successes and failures
steps.instruction: Upload the workbook or ZIP. The page shows successful, failed and remaining rows as processing continues. Download results. Read failure reasons, correct only failed rows, then retry them without uploading successful rows again.
steps.note: A failed row should not partially save. Results contain success.xlsx and failure.xlsx; referenced local image files are retained for retry.

steps.title: Start a sales bill
steps.instruction: In Sales and Quotations, choose the customer. Add a missing customer using the button provided. Check the invoice date, billing address, store and place of supply before adding what you sold.
steps.note: Use a real customer record for credit sales so later collections can be matched.

steps.title: Choose products and quantities
steps.instruction: Select Steel water bottle, enter quantity two and price two hundred and fifty rupees. Our sample sale totals five hundred rupees with GST off. Check the complete bill total before posting.
steps.note: The example prices are made up. Registered businesses must check the applicable GST and place of supply.

steps.title: Record only what was received
steps.instruction: The customer pays three hundred rupees now. Enter that in Amount Received Now, choose cash as the payment mode and Shop cash as the receiving account. Two hundred rupees is still due.
steps.note: Do not enter the full bill amount unless you actually received it. A payment mode describes how; the account says where the money went.

steps.title: Keep track of the unpaid part
steps.instruction: Keep Auto-create receivable selected for the unpaid balance. Review the bill, then choose Post Invoice once. Later, record the remaining two hundred rupees in Receivables and Collections, against this bill.
steps.note: A posted bill affects records and stock. Correct mistakes using the supported cancellation or reversal flow rather than posting a duplicate.

steps.title: Check the stock after a sale
steps.instruction: Back in Product Inventory, check stock by store and Stock History. We began with twenty-four bottles and sold two, so twenty-two remain. The history explains which movement changed the quantity.
steps.note: If the quantity is unexpected, inspect the movements instead of adding another opening balance.

steps.title: Choose what customers can see
steps.instruction: For a product to appear online, keep it active and select Visible in customer catalog. Check the name, price, photo and available variants. Save your changes, then view the shop as a customer.
steps.note: Published catalogue items still need valid prices and available owned stock for online purchase. An enquiry is different from checkout.

steps.title: Make the website your own
steps.instruction: In Company Setup, open Storefront Design. Choose a theme, pictures and wording. Selected products, brands and categories come first; the rest follow unless you explicitly choose Show only selected. Preview before saving.
steps.note: Open the storefront only when your public contact details, policies and catalogue are ready. Keep business access separate from shopper access.

steps.title: Share your own online shop
steps.instruction: Share your Tenali shop link with customers. They can browse products and pictures on their phone, choose variants and ask about items. Your website is connected to the same product and stock records.
steps.note: Mobile shelves scroll sideways. Prices, stock and enabled checkout methods determine what a customer can buy.

steps.title: Let customers send a WhatsApp list
steps.instruction: Customers can collect several items into a WhatsApp enquiry list and send quantities together. Use it to discuss bulk prices or availability. A WhatsApp conversation does not create a paid order or reserve stock.
steps.note: Set the business phone in Company Setup. Enquiries can stay available when checkout is off. Do not treat an enquiry as confirmed payment.

steps.title: Connect online payments
steps.instruction: To accept online purchases, open Payments and Delivery Setup and connect your own Razorpay account. Start in Test Mode, complete the setup and checks, then use approved live credentials for real customer payments.
steps.note: Provider approval, keys, automatic capture and webhook setup are separate requirements. Never share keys or secrets in chat. The tutorial does not connect or charge a provider account.

steps.title: Choose how orders are delivered
steps.instruction: Choose your own delivery team or courier, or connect Shiprocket using its dedicated API user and pickup location. Confirm delivery coverage and charges. Online Orders is where you process orders and record dispatch or collection.
steps.note: Shiprocket is optional and needs its own setup and approval. Booking a shipment does not prove delivery. Track cash-on-delivery receipts separately where applicable.

steps.title: Use a domain you own
steps.instruction: For your own web address, open Storefront Domains. Add a domain you own, follow the displayed DNS instructions and verify it. Keep your email records intact. Your existing Tenali shop link remains available. You can return to any chapter whenever you need a reminder.
steps.note: A domain is your website's address. You arrange domain ownership; DNS and HTTPS changes can take time. Features depend on enabled services and your role. Thank you for exploring Tenali.
